name: Poisson-Visser thin-shell linearised radial stability: equation of motion Rdot^2 = -V(R), conservation law, beta^2 = dp/dsigma parametrisation, stability iff V'' > 0

source.located: E. Poisson & M. Visser, 'Thin-shell wormholes: Linearization stability', arXiv:gr-qc/9506083v1 (30 Jun 1995), Phys. Rev. D 52, 7318 (1995), 4 pp. Eqs (1)-(2) cut-and-paste of TWO copies of Schwarzschild with the SAME M; (6)-(8) Lanczos/Israel surface stress; (11)-(12) sigma, p of the throat; (13)/(15) conservation; (14)-(17) adot^2 = -V(a), V = 1 - 2M/a - [2 pi sigma(a) a]^2; (18)-(19) static sigma0, p0; (23) beta^2 = dp/dsigma; (26)-(29) V'' and 'stable if and only if'; (30)-(36) stability regions; sec IV caveats on beta as sound speed. Companion sources read for the parts of the tree's use that are NOT in PV: Ishak & Lake, arXiv:gr-qc/0108058v2 (PRD 65, 044011, 2002) eq (5) (the two-mass equation of motion, credited there to Lake 1979), eqs (6)-(8),(12) transparency, (14)-(19) stability; Pitre, Schneider & Poisson, arXiv:2604.05980v1 (2026) eqs (3.11)-(3.17) (Minkowski-inside/Schwarzschild-outside radial criterion Gamma_1, citing LeMaitre & Poisson, Am. J. Phys. 87, 961 (2019)). Brady-Louko-Poisson PRD 44, 1891 (1991) (PV's ref [6], the Minkowski/Schwarzschild-type shell PV say they 'follow closely'), Lake PRD 19, 2847 (1979) and LeMaitre-Poisson 2019 are NAMED-NOT-READ.

published_statement: PV eq (17): 'adot^2 = -V(a); V(a) = 1 - 2M/a - [2 pi sigma(a) a]^2. This single dynamical equation completely determines the motion of the wormhole throat.' Eq (15): 'sigma_dot = -2(sigma + p) adot/a.' Eq (23): 'beta^2(sigma) = dp/dsigma ... The physical interpretation of beta is a matter of some subtlety ... For now, we simply consider beta to be a useful parameter related to the equation of state.' Eq (27): V''(a0) = -2 a0^-2 [2M/a0 + (M^2/a0^2)/(1 - 2M/a0) + (1 + 2 beta0^2)(1 - 3M/a0)]. Eq (28)-(29): 'The equation of motion for the wormhole throat is, at this order of approximation, adot^2 = -(1/2) V''(a0)[a - a0]^2 + O([a - a0]^3). So for V''(a0) > 0 the wormhole is stable, while for V''(a0) < 0 perturbations can grow (at least until the nonlinear regime is reached). Thus the wormhole is stable if and only if: [(29)] < 0.' Regions (35)-(36): I: beta0^2 >= 3/2 + sqrt3, a0- < a0 < a0+; II: beta0^2 <= -1/2, a0 > a0-; unstable for all a0 when -1/2 < beta0^2 < 3/2 + sqrt3. Sec IV: 'there is no guarantee that beta0 actually is the speed of sound ... wormhole configurations with |beta0^2| > 1 should not be ruled out a priori.'
published_hypotheses: H1 configuration: two copies of Schwarzschild with the same mass M, each with r <= a (a > 2M) removed, boundaries identified (eqs 1-2) -- a symmetric thin-shell WORMHOLE, both sides exterior, so sigma0 < 0 (eq 18, 'exotic matter')
H2 infinitesimally thin shell; Lanczos/Sen/Israel junction (eqs 3-8), G = c = 1
H3 spherical symmetry preserved: only radial (spherically symmetric) perturbations, a -> a(tau) (abstract; sec II)
H4 vacuum (Schwarzschild) on both sides, so no flux onto the shell and the conservation law (13)/(15) is exact
H5 barotropic equation of state p = p(sigma), integrated formally via (16); only its slope beta0^2 at the static point enters V''(a0)
H6 an ASSUMED static solution (a0, sigma0, p0) inter-related by (18)-(19); V(a0) = V'(a0) = 0
H7 linearised (second-order-in-V) analysis: 'at this order of approximation'; V''(a0) > 0 stable, < 0 unstable 'at least until the nonlinear regime is reached'; V'' = 0 not classified
H8 beta is a parameter, NOT asserted to be a sound speed; no microphysical model of the matter (sec IV)
hypothesis_drift: CONFIGURATION / ATTRIBUTION (discrepancy, not refutation): PV treat ONLY the symmetric Schwarzschild wormhole (H1; M equal on both sides; their V is eq 17). The tree cites PV for the TWO-MASS potential V = 1 - 2M_out/R - [dM/m_s - m_s/2R]^2 (stability.py:40-42) and for V = 1 - [m_s/(2R) + m/m_s]^2 with Minkowski inside, Schwarzschild outside (wall.py:222-225, V_of_R wall.py:327-330). Neither formula is in PV. The two-mass form is Ishak-Lake gr-qc/0108058 eq (5) with the MEAN mass mbar = (M_in+M_out)/2 (credited there to Lake 1979), and the Minkowski/Schwarzschild ordinary shell is the configuration of Brady-Louko-Poisson 1991 (PV's ref [6]) / LeMaitre-Poisson 2019 / PSP 2026. Both are re-derived here from the Israel junction and hold exactly (rederive block A); what the tree takes from PV is the METHOD (conservation integration, beta^2 parametrisation, V'' > 0), which carries over unchanged.

ADDED HYPOTHESIS, negative interior mass: stability.py:17-20, 40, 150-193 generalises to M_in = -m < 0, M_out = 0. Not in PV (H1) and not among Ishak-Lake's examples. The algebra is valid for any M_in with f_in = 1 - 2M_in/R > 0 (automatic for M_in < 0), and the rederivation reproduces every stability.py number. The owner flags this generalisation in its own hypothesis list (canonical entry). Hypotheses it rests on that the tree should NAME and does not at these lines: (a) the region between core and shell is exact vacuum Schwarzschild with mass parameter -m and static (Ishak-Lake's transparency condition eq 12: m = m(R), no flux) -- at l = 0 this is Birkhoff; (b) the r = 0 of negative-mass Schwarzschild is singular, i.e. the 'core' is idealised (irrelevant at l = 0, relevant for any l >= 1 work the file lists as NOT RUN).

DROPPED HYPOTHESIS, orientation signs lost on squaring: PV's (11) carries a definite sign (sigma < 0 from both normals pointing away); the squared potential (PV 17, tree stability.py:40, wall.py:224) no longer records which sign branch the shell is on. The tree's ordinary shell and device need A = sqrt(f_in + Rdot^2) = dM/m_s + m_s/2R > 0 and B = sqrt(f_out + Rdot^2) = dM/m_s - m_s/2R > 0. Not stated at stability.py:40-42 or wall.py:222-225; checked here to hold at the static points of the device (m/R = 0.01, 1) and the ordinary shell (M/R = 0.1) (rederive block F), so it does not move the l = 0 conclusion. It bounds any finite-amplitude use: V reaches its ceiling 1 exactly where B = 0 (block G).

WEAKENED QUALIFIER, 'linearised' dropped from the verdict: PV's result is linear (H7, eq 28 'at this order of approximation'; title 'Linearization stability'). wall.py keeps it ('the linearised radial mode is strictly stable iff', wall.py:22-23). stability.py's headline and verdict say 'RADIALLY STABLE WITH NO PRESSURE RESPONSE AT ALL' (stability.py:11-13, 255-258, 306-309) without 'linearly'. Scope measured here (block G): for the device at beta^2 = 0 the closed-form V(R) has no barrier top between R/R0 = 0.0048 and 21 at m/R = 0.01 (0.0435 to 21 at 0.10; 0.148 to 9.41 at 0.50), so the dropped word does not hide a narrow basin -- but the claim proved is the linear one.

ADDED HYPOTHESIS, globally constant beta^2: PV need only beta0^2 at the static point (H5). wall.py:226-229 integrates sigma(R) in closed form for a GLOBALLY linear EOS (A = 1 + beta^2, K = p0 - beta^2 sigma0) and uses it for the period checks and the 'BONUS' unbounded dominant-energy basin (wall.py:204-219), which is a finite/infinite-amplitude statement outside PV's linear scope. The owner names 'linear surface equation of state (beta^2 constant)' as a hypothesis (canonical entry), so this is carried, not dropped; the V''(R0) and beta2_crit results do not depend on it.

KEPT, beta^2 not a sound speed: PV sec IV (H8). wall.py names it: 'beta^2 here is the slope of the thin-shell surface equation of state, which is not identical to the microphysical sound speed ... The causality reading beta^2 <= 1 is the standard one and is a proxy' (wall.py, caveat 3 before 'A BONUS THEOREM'). stability.py:62-64 claims only that any beta^2 >= 0 clears a negative beta2_crit, which needs no sound-speed reading. No drift.

KEPT, l = 0 only: PV H3. stability.py:79-92, 283-292 lists l >= 2 and l = 1 as NOT RUN; wall.py:128-150 records PSP 2026's l >= 2 even-parity instability and withdraws part of its conclusion. No drift.

NUMERICAL METHOD (owner-added, not a PV hypothesis): stability.py:162-182 computes V'' by a central second difference (h = 1e-5) with m_s integrated by a 200-step midpoint rule and beta2_crit by bisection on [-3, 10]. Every printed value agrees with the exact closed form at its printed precision (block E), and the bisection root is unique because V''(R0) is affine in beta^2 (beta^2 enters only through m_s''); no drift in outcome.

A: from A - B = m_s/R and A^2 - B^2 = f_in - f_out the tree's two-mass V (stability.py:40) follows exactly; it equals Ishak-Lake eq (5) with the MEAN mass (and differs by dM/R if m is read as M_out); M_in = 0 gives wall.py's V exactly; PV (11) squared gives PV (17). B: PV (11),(12) imply (13) and (15) symbolically; m_s' = -8 pi R p exact. C: PV (26) at (18),(19) equals (27); an independent V''(a0) from V(a) and (15) equals (27); V(a0) = V'(a0) = 0; the V'' = 0 boundary numerator is exactly 2 x PV (33); discriminant 4b^2 - 12b - 3, roots 3/2 -+ sqrt3; (31) RHS -> -1/2 as a0 -> infinity and the region-I boundary minimum is exactly 3/2 + sqrt3. D: V(R0) = V'(R0) = 0 identically in beta^2 for general (M_in, M_out); the independent V'' equals wall.py's Vpp symbolically; beta2_crit(x) = (1-s)(3s^2+2s+1)/(4s^2(1+3s)) exactly; beta2_crit(2/3) = (sqrt3-1)/2 and (4/5) = sqrt5 - 3/2 exactly; beta2_crit(0.3) = 0.079332; beta2_crit = 1 <=> 15s^3+3s^2-s-1 = 0, x* = 0.843741892629; PSP 2026 Gamma_1 (eq 3.16b) times p/(mu+p) equals wall.py's beta2_crit exactly -- an independent 2026 source. E: device V''(beta^2=0) exact +2.965589e-2, +2.700655e-1, +1.017767e0 (tree +2.965e-2, +2.700e-1, +1.018e0); ordinary -3.035611e-2, -3.423762e-1, -8.169356e-1 (tree -3.036e-2, -3.424e-1, -8.169e-1); device beta2_crit = -(w-1)(3w^2+2w+1)/(4w^2(3w+1)), w = sqrt(1+2m/R) -- the mirror of wall.py's formula under s -> w; exact -0.003680 at 0.01 and -0.132561 at 1.0 (tree -0.0037, -0.132); z3 proves -1/4 < beta2_crit(device) < 0 for EVERY m/R > 0 (vacuity guard sat). The 'near mirror' ratio (V''ord + V''dev)/|V''ord| = -0.02307 at 0.01 (tree tolerance 0.03); at 0.10 the magnitudes differ by 21 % -- 'NEARLY' is accurate at low compactness only, as the tree's own table shows. F: orientation signs A, B > 0 hold at the static points. G: finite-amplitude well at beta^2 = 0 is wide (no barrier top for 0.0048 < R/R0 < 21 at m/R = 0.01). Recorded PV-internal discrepancies (not used by the tree, not refutations): (36) prints 'beta0^2 <= -1/2' where no finite a0 is stable at exactly -1/2 (strict '<'); sec IV writes the Casimir slope as 'beta^2 = d sigma/d p = -1', which for p = -sigma equals dp/dsigma = -1 anyway. The owners' own selftests (python3 stability.py --selftest; python3 wall.py --selftest) both print SELFTEST OK.

later_literature.what: Generalises PV to arbitrary enveloping spherically symmetric spacetimes, M_in != M_out (eq 5, 'the equation of motion ... applies to both shells and wormholes'), with the transparency condition (6)/(12) as the explicit extra hypothesis, and reproduces PV exactly in its sec III.A (eq 21). This -- not PV -- is the published home of the two-mass V the tree uses at stability.py:40; verified equal to it with mbar = (M_in+M_out)/2.

later_literature.ref: T. Pitre, B. Schneider & E. Poisson, arXiv:2604.05980 (2026), 'Self-gravitating thin shells are dynamically unstable on all angular scales'
later_literature.what: For Minkowski-inside/Schwarzschild-outside barotropic shells (wall.py's configuration; not stability.py's M_in < 0 one) confirms the radial criterion Gamma >= Gamma_1 = (1+2sqrt F+3F)/(4F) (eq 3.16b; maximum-mass turning point = onset of radial instability, citing LeMaitre-Poisson 2019) -- equal to wall.py's beta2_crit exactly (block D) -- and then shows an even-parity mode with positive imaginary frequency for every sampled compactness, adiabatic index and l >= 2. PV-type radial stability therefore does not imply stability for this class. This does not falsify PV's l = 0 statement; it narrows what 'stable' may be read to mean. The tree already carries this (wall.py:128-150; stability.py:79-92 lists l >= 2 as the top NOT-RUN risk for the M_in < 0 device, to which PSP's configuration does not directly apply).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested: what did Poisson and Visser lack, and would having it change the conclusion? PV name the gap themselves (sec IV): 'a detailed microphysical model for the exotic matter would be necessary' to know whether beta0 is a sound speed, and so whether the stable regions (beta0^2 <= -1/2 or >= 3/2 + sqrt3) are physically reachable. That lack bears on PV's PHYSICAL reading of the wormhole regions, not on the mathematics of V, the conservation law or the V'' > 0 criterion, which contain no measured datum at all and are re-derived exactly here. Nothing learned since 1995 moves them: Ishak-Lake 2002 generalise them, Eiroa et al. 2024 use them unchanged, and PSP 2026 reproduce the equivalent radial criterion for the Minkowski/Schwarzschild shell exactly. What PV did lack -- and what later work supplied -- is the NON-RADIAL spectrum: PSP 2026 show an l >= 2 instability for positive-mass, Minkowski-inside shells at every sampled compactness and adiabatic index. That is additional information that changes what 'stable' may be claimed to mean for a thin shell, but it does not contradict PV's l = 0 linear statement, and the tree already carries it. For the tree's own use the relevant missing 'data' is not external at all: the negative-mass interior of stability.py has no physical realisation and no later literature was found on it (discovery call not possible), so its l >= 1 stability is OPEN -- which stability.py itself says. Evidence either way: no moved datum; no contradiction computed; one piece of later physics (l >= 2) that narrows the reading and is already recorded.
grade_evidence: Every formula the tree takes from or attributes to this result is re-derived independently and agrees exactly (45/45 checks): the tree's two-mass V and wall.py's Minkowski-inside V follow from the Israel junction; m_s' = -8 pi R p follows from PV (11)-(15); V(R0) = V'(R0) = 0 identically in beta^2; the independent V'' equals wall.py's closed form symbolically and reproduces PV's own (27), (33), (34) and the 3/2 +- sqrt3 and -1/2 boundaries; every number printed at stability.py:47-64 and wall.py:28-40 is reproduced at its printed precision; z3 proves beta2_crit(device) in (-1/4, 0) for all m/R > 0, so the stability.py verdict holds on the whole compactness range, not only the sampled one; PSP 2026 (read) gives an equivalent radial criterion that equals wall.py's beta2_crit exactly. No empirical datum enters, so none can move. Carried with the grade, not grade-moving: (1) ATTRIBUTION DISCREPANCY -- PV's published class is the symmetric wormhole only; the two-mass V (stability.py:40) is Ishak-Lake eq (5)/Lake 1979, and the Minkowski/Schwarzschild shell (wall.py:222) is Brady-Louko-Poisson's/LeMaitre-Poisson's configuration; the formulas are right, the citation is to the method's originator rather than to the formula's. (2) UNNAMED HYPOTHESES the tree satisfies but should name at stability.py:40-42 / wall.py:222-225: the orientation signs lost on squaring (verified true at the static points) and, for stability.py, a static vacuum negative-mass Schwarzschild interior (Birkhoff at l = 0). (3) 'linearly' is dropped from stability.py's verdict wording (stability.py:11-13, 255-258); the claim proved is PV's linear l = 0 one, and the measured beta^2 = 0 well is wide. None of these shrinks the class on which the tree's l = 0 linear conclusion holds, so the grade is not NARROWED; STANDS means LINEAR RADIAL (l = 0) stability in PV's sense and nothing more -- PSP 2026 show that for positive-mass shells it does not imply full stability, which the tree already records.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the tree's radial verdict were read (or quoted) as unqualified stability rather than linear l = 0 stability, or if a finite-amplitude use crossed the B = 0 orientation boundary where the squared V stops describing the configuration; NARROWED (for stability.py only) if the negative-mass interior were shown not to be a static vacuum Schwarzschild region at the shell (e.g. a dynamical or extended core, breaking Birkhoff/transparency). WRONG only on a computed contradiction to the junction algebra or conservation law, and none exists (45/45). OPEN would replace STANDS if the cached text of gr-qc/9506083 were shown not to be the arXiv v1 (re-read at alphaXiv when the quota resets and compare md5 of the page text) -- the Ishak-Lake and PSP cross-checks would still stand independently.
